newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Employment in government and local authorities grew last year in sharp contrast to the private sector, which again shed jobs after a bried respite in 1995.
- HIV infection in South Africa had soared last year to the level where 14,07 percent of women attending antenatal clinics were infected, Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma said on Thursday.

- Broking firm Smith Borkum Hare (SBH), now wholly owned by US-based Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, has lost the entire small client arm of its corporate finance department with the departure of an SBH director and three consultants to start their own firm.

- Mpumalanga government officials quashed an internal investigation of allegations that the issuing of a learner's and driver's licence to parliamentary deputy speaker Baleka Kgositsile was irregurlar, the Moldenhauer inquiry heard on Thursday.

- Two policemen sent to the African National Congress' Johannesburg headquarters to guard spent AK-47 cartridges on the day of the Shell House shootings had to jump off a balcony to escape about 20 ANC security guards, a judicial inquest.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Arms exports from South Africa to India and Saudi Arabia, worth more than four billion rand, are either close to being concluded or are under discussion, industry sources said.

- Weak bullion prices and poor productivity could lead to the closure of four shafts and 10,000 job losses at Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd unit, Anglo said on Thursday as it announced a 34 percent fall in group profit for the quarter.

- Inefficiencies in the customs and excise department cost the country an estimated 17 billion rand a year, Gill Marcus, the finance deputy minister, told the international conference on economic policy issues held in Durban.

- Sun International (South Africa) Ltd, the casino and hotel conglomerate, has joined forces with a Western Cape- based empowerment consortium to lauch Sun West International, a fledgling leisure industry offshoot.

- Telkom's international inquiries service will no longer be free from May 1 because of the growing number of obscene and nuisance calls, Geoff Merryweather, Telkom's head of maritime and international operations, said on Thursday.
THE STAR

- Bafana Bafana coach Clive Barker dropped a bombshell on Thursday when he hinted that he may not continue coaching the national soccer team after the final World Cup qualifying match against Congo at Johannesburg's FNB stadium on August 16.

- Senior Mpumalanga government officials quashed an internal investigationinto allegations that the issuing of a learner's and driver's licence to parliamentary Deputy Speaker Baleka Kgositsile was irregular, the Moldenhauer inquiry heard.

- Four men masquerading as lawyers were arrested at the Thohoyandou police station in the Northern Province when they demanded to visit men held in connection with this week's 4.6 million rand highway robbery.

- The life and times of Josia Thugwane, South Africa's Olympic marathon gold medallist, will soon be captured on celluloid according his coach Jacques Malan who disclosed that plans were at an advanced stage for a major U.S.-produced docu- drama about the champion's rags-to-riches story.
